| **2611.02289** | Thirty years of primordial deuterium abundances: A provenance-aware statistical reanalysis | Builds a 957-entry, 247-publication provenance-aware D/H database (1994–2026) and finds the "modern consensus" D/H ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ is driven by only ~16 effectively-independent absorbers (HHI measure) out of 52 identified — most literature values are reused/compiled rather than new. ### Modified Gravity / Dark Energy (Horndeski N-body — notable cluster this week)

| arXiv ID | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| **2611.06330** | Horndeski Gravity as an Effective Dark Energy Fluid in Cosmological N-body Simulations | Patches `CONCEPT` (N-body, CLASS-based) with `mochi_CLASS` to evolve linear Horndeski DE perturbations as an effective fluid; validates on w₀wₐCDM, Hu-Sawicki f(R), and cubic Galileon + massive neutrinos. Finds up to 40% deviation from GR for f(R), <25% for cubic Galileon. **First CONCEPT+Horndeski implementation** — a new nonlinear MG N-body code to add to our `03_modified_gravity_dark_energy.md` tools table. |
| **2611.03637** | Mercury (Hg): a relativistic N-body simulation for Horndeski gravity | New relativistic PM N-body code implementing the full Horndeski α-basis (α_K, α_B, α_M, α_T), validated against hi_class in the linear regime; demonstrated on nKGB, Cubic Galileon, Brans-Dicke. Positioned as "intermediate step toward nonlinear Horndeski simulations." Two independent Horndeski N-body codes released in the same week (Mercury + CONCEPT/Horndeski above) — the nonlinear-MG-simulation space is maturing fast. Both are strong integration candidates for our proposed `modified-gravity-mcp-server`'s `compute_mg_power_spectrum` tool. |
| **2611.05089 / 2611.05112** | Scale-dependent weak-field Horndeski dynamics (galaxy rotation curves); Horndeski without dark matter (Refracted Gravity limit) | Two galactic-scale Horndeski papers this week probing whether scalar-tensor gravity can replace DM on small scales — tangential to our cosmological-scale focus but worth a one-line mention for completeness of the Horndeski literature map. |

No new f(R)-specific emulator or DESI-neutrino-mass-emulator papers appeared in the 7-day window (queries for "modified gravity emulator", "f(R) gravity emulator", and direct DESI+neutrino-mass combos returned nothing dated this week) — the DESI/dark-energy query surfaced mostly galactic/CGM/IA papers using DESI data rather than new cosmological-constraint methodology.

### AI Agents for Physics / MCP for Science

| arXiv ID | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| **2611.06910** | FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research | New, harder benchmark than prior week's entries: 56 tasks from 42 physicists' own research across 9 domains (theory/computational/experimental), requiring literature review → research plan → execution → structured manuscript output. **Across 22 models / 26 configs, no configuration passed more than 46/168 rollouts (~27% best case).** Diagnosis: agents' main failure mode is "insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition," not knowledge or execution gaps. This is the most direct, quantitative confirmation yet of the theme flagged in our `06_ai_agents_multiscale_physics.md` (PhysClosureBench, 2610.21767) — the open problem is scoping/closing real research, not raw calculation. Strongly motivates continuing to track our own `hep-genesis-alpha-test` harness correctness-bug log as a complementary, in-house data point. |
| **2611.03373 (v2)** | Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in HEP: Monte Carlo Case Study | LLM agent reproduces a published CEPC Bell-observable analysis (e+e⁻→ZH, H→ZZ*→4μ) under human supervision; finds value less in faster code generation, more in faster *scientific iteration* (workflow planning, anomaly diagnosis, control construction). Proposes systematic benchmarking via correctness/intervention/researcher-time metrics — directly comparable framing to our own harness tracking. |
| **2610.41717** | Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments (instrMCP + q-devBench) | New MCP server (`instrMCP`) connecting AI agents to real lab instruments via QCoDeS/QMeasure, with a benchmark (q-devBench) for live hardware control tasks. Extends the "MCP enters experimental hardware control" trend flagged 2026-10-08 (ARTIQ trapped-ion MCP) to a general condensed-matter table-top instrument stack. Second MCP-hardware-control paper tracked within a month — this is now a recognizable sub-trend worth its own watch-item in `06_ai_agents_multiscale_physics.md`. |

3. **MCP-hardware-control sub-trend**: instrMCP (this week) + ARTIQ MCP (10/08) suggest a maturing "MCP for lab instrument control" niche distinct from our compute/simulation-focused servers. Worth a short watch-item in `06_ai_agents_multiscale_physics.md` even though it's outside our current scope (no immediate action needed).
4. Continue tracking FrontierPhysics-style end-to-end benchmarks (now 3 in 4 weeks: PhysClosureBench, Wellocate/explore-confirm, FrontierPhysics) as external validation data for our own agent-harness correctness bugs — consider writing up `hep-genesis-alpha-test`'s bug log against FrontierPhysics' 20-criterion Atomic Score rubric as a comparison exercise.
